english: In that year it did not rain. The spring dried up. Grief seized the man's heart. The heat was burning the field and the cattle were thirsty. He raised his two hands and spoke: "Father Sky, where is the water? Give us rain!" Then Dyeus heard him. Thunder came and a cloud rose up. It rained. The cattle ran to the spring and drank. He rejoiced.
uncertain: swóh₁ ǵʰóstoh₁: INS.SG or ACC.DU; read as ACC.DU 'his two hands' as object of tl̥néh₂t
tl̥néh₂t: PST (imperfective) 'was lifting', read as 'raised'
bʰréh₁wr̥: bare accusative of goal 'to the spring'

english: When night has come, the cattle come (home). The cheerful woman, standing in the enclosure, milks them. Her daughter milks the sheep. They give much. She says: "Cows, stand!" They stand still. The man is sitting. No one comes. They lay down. They were sated.
uncertain: gʷówes sth₂éh₁yete: VOC.PL + 2PL (PRS/PST/IMP); read as command inside her speech
dédh₃n̥ti: 3PL subject unexpressed; taken as the milked animals
l̥gʰént, sh₂ént: AOR 3PL after present-tense narration; subject taken as the animals

english: Dawn grew bright. The shepherd was leading the cattle out of the cow-stall. The swift goat went ahead, and the sheep and the horse followed. They were making their way to the field. They ate. He sat down and kept watching them. Then he drove them to the spring and they drank. They were sated. When night came, he drove them into the enclosure.
uncertain: h₁r̥sḱónt: PST.3PL or participle; read as finite 'were going to'
h₁éy: anaphoric NOM.SG 'he' (the shepherd), not the imperative 'go'

english: Oxen, pull! Pull the plough! Bear the yoke! Make the furrow straight! Do not stray! The heat burns and we sweat. The man follows you. I sow the seed. May Mother Earth give grain. May the sun warm the seed. Oxen, pull!
uncertain: dukté, bʰérete, h₃roǵéyete: 2PL PRS/PST/IMP ambiguous; read as imperatives addressed to the oxen (gʷówes VOC.PL)
séh₁yoh₂: 1SG while the previous sentence has 1PL; speaker taken as the singer/sower
sékʷetor: MID.PRS.3SG 'follows' (or SBJV of sékʷt)

english: Sky, our father, giver of good things, hear! Now this field is dry. Mother Earth is thirsty. You who slew the great serpent, give us water! You who split the great cloud, rain on the field! May thunder come, may the grain swell. May good grain grow for us, may the spring fill. May the horses and goats drink. May the apples turn red.
uncertain: h₁uséwōm: GEN.PL 'of goods' governed by déh₃tor
h₁wésu: neuter, taken as agreeing with ǵr̥h₂nóm 'good grain'
misfit: gʷʰéns: PST.2SG of imperfective gʷʰénti 'was slaying' for a completed mythic deed; the parallel relative clause uses AOR bʰéyds, so an aorist is expected here too

english: "Let it be so," said the bright god Werunos.
uncertain: tód h₁estu: IMP.3SG of 'be' (h₁ést 'throw' also possible but senseless here)
wérunos: not in the lexicon; read as a divine name in apposition (cf. Varuna)
misfit: wérunos: no analysis at all from the analyzer and no lexicon entry; looks like a theonym the lexicon does not cover

english: A guest arrived at night. The master said: "Guest, come inside! Sit at the hearth! Eat and drink!" A guest is dear in the house. "Who are you?" The guest said: "A wild beast seized my sheep, and I fled." The master said: "May the gods give you good things."
uncertain: bʰéwgm̥: AOR.1SG 'I fled' (homonym 'benefit' also listed); 1SG implies direct speech by the guest
gʰóstis démi lewbʰós h₁ésti: could be the master's words or a narrator's maxim
h₂ówins: possessor unexpressed; 'my' supplied

english: Son, know your sheep! Lead the cattle to the spring! If a sheep goes missing, search for it. Do not leave them in the dark. The dog is your eye in the dark. If a wild beast comes, cry out to the dog. Do not be afraid. Whoever stays awake guards his sheep.
uncertain: tóns: masc ACC.PL; the sheep are feminine here (h₁íh₂m̥, swā́s), so 'them' is taken as the herd as a whole (cattle are masc.)
h₁régʷesi: LOC.SG 'in the dark' (also SBJV.2SG of unglossed h₁régʷti)
leléykʷeti: SBJV of the perfect 'be missing'

english: It was getting dark. Sheep, lie down! Cattle, lie down! The watchman is awake. The fire glows red. May sleep take you. May no wild beast come. May it not see them. He stays on watch.
uncertain: h₂wéseti: PRS 'dwells, remains' (the watchman) or SBJV of h₂wést 'dawn shall come'
h₁éy: masc 'he' = the beast; h₁íh₂n̥s fem.pl = the sheep
l̥gʰté: AOR.2PL or IMP.2PL; read as imperative

english: Then the king's wife bore a son.
uncertain: h₃réḱs: read as GEN.SG 'king's' (NOM also possible, but then no link to pótnih₂)
ǵeǵonh₁e: PRF 'has been born' is intransitive
misfit: ǵeǵonh₁e: intransitive perfect 'is/has been born' cannot take ACC súHnum as its object; expected NOM suHnús ('a son was born to...') or a transitive 'beget/bear' verb

english: Let us cut the ears of grain. Let us carry the load. Work with many hands is quick. The heat burns and the wheat is dry. The apples are red. Let us eat the apples and the onions. Let us sing a hymn. Dear one, drink mead! Sister, eat grain! Let us rejoice.
uncertain: méwdomes: SBJV.1PL of méwdt or PRS.1PL; read as hortative
wósh₂r̥: garlic/onion
h₂éboln̥s-kʷe: -kʷe on the first word, read as a clause link

english: Earth, shelter your offspring in your arms. Now we sow seed for you. Give us grain, grant us wheat. May it grow for us, may it not die. May the roots be firm, may the onions swell. May the ears of wheat be many. May the onions grow, may the shoot spring from the root.
uncertain: ḱéle: IMP of 'be covering, hiding'; read as 'shelter'
h₁íd: neuter, taken as the seed (séh₁mn̥)
wr̥h₂dés: GEN or ABL; read as ABL 'from the root'

english: "Father, who nourishes the field?" "Water nourishes it." "Who nourishes the water?" "Sky nourishes it." "Who nourishes Sky?" "No one. He is our father."
uncertain: kʷís: NOM.SG interrogative, needs a 3SG verb
ne kʷis h₁ésti: literally 'there is no one'
misfit: h₂élomes: 1PL 'we nourish' does not agree with subject kʷís (NOM.SG); the parallel questions use h₂életi, so expected h₂életi ('who nourishes the field?')

english: The adorned bride was coming to the hearth. She walked around it. Her mother wept and said: "Daughter, be dear to your husband!" Her brother gave her a gift of gold. Her husband gave her honey. She ate it. Then he said: "Wife, be the mistress of this house! May your sons be many. May the hearth stand firm."
uncertain: h₁íh₂m̥: fem ACC = the hearth (h₂éHsh₂ fem)
h₁íd: neuter = the honey
HréwdHt: PST 'was weeping' beside AOR h₂éǵt

english: Gods, protect the cattle and the sheep! Protect the goats and the horses! May they live and be many. May the bear not seize them at night. May the watchman stay awake, and may ram and goat live. May they see the dawn!
uncertain: h₂léksete: 2PL PRS/PST/IMP; read as imperative to deywṓs (VOC.PL)
moysós-kʷe kápros: two singular subjects with 3PL verb; -kʷe read as clause link
-ge: emphatic
misfit: polh₁ús: NOM.SG adjective as predicate of 3PL h₁sih₁ént 'may they be'; expected NOM.PL polh₁éwes

english: The master's son was driving the sheep to the pasture. He cried out: "A wild beast has come!" The men from over there arrived. They saw nothing. He was delighted. Three times he fooled them. Then the beast really did come. He cried out, and no one heard him. It seized the sheep. Whoever deceives, no one listens to him.
uncertain: h₁éy: masc 'he' = the beast (ǵʰwḗr masc); h₁íh₂n̥s fem.pl = sheep
h₂én: 'yonder', read as 'from over there'
trís: 'thrice'

english: Dawn, adorned daughter of Sky, shine! You who drove away the great darkness, lead the cattle out of the cow-stall to the pasture! May they live and be many. May they see you, and may the sun follow you.
uncertain: h₂éwsos: VOC of h₂éwsōs (also GEN of 'ear', senseless here)
sékʷetor: MID.PRS.3SG 'follows' or MID.SBJV.3SG of sékʷt; read as a wish to match the optatives
te ... te: enclitic 'you' twice, not 'both...and'
misfit: polh₁ús: NOM.SG as predicate of 3PL h₁sih₁ént; expected NOM.PL polh₁éwes

english: It was getting dark. The man and the woman lay down. Sleep seized the two of them. The fire glowed red. The dog lay by the hearth, stayed awake, and guarded the pair. A bird called. It grew light. He got up.
uncertain: h₂nḗr-kʷe gʷḗn: -kʷe on the first conjunct; read as 'and' joining to the previous sentence or the pair
stéh₂t: 3SG with no subject; the man or the dog
h₂éwis: NOM 'bird' (GEN of 'sheep' also possible but no head noun)

english: It was getting dark. Thunder was coming. Then a cloud rose overhead. The barley was trembling. The man was standing in the field. Trembling, he cried out: "Cloud, do not break the ears of grain! Go away!" It heard him. It went away and did not break them. It grew light. They were untouched. He was astonished and rejoiced.
uncertain: h₁éy (in 'h₁éy h₁ím ḱléwt' / 'h₁éy h₂epó gʷéh₂t'): masc = the cloud (n̥bʰrós)
h₁íh₂: neut ACC.PL = the ears (h₂éḱōs, neut)
misfit: n̥th₂grṓs: masc NOM.PL, but its subject must be the ears of grain (h₂éḱōs, neuter, resumed by neut.pl h₁íh₂); expected neut.pl n̥th₂gréh₂. The 3PL h₁sént points the same way: neuter plural subjects take a 3SG verb elsewhere (12a83cac h₂éḱōs polh₁úh₂ h₁syéh₁t)

english: Three dear guests were arriving. The master seated them at the hearth. His wife cooked wheat and onions and served them round. They ate it all and drank mead three times. They were satisfied. He said: "May Father Sky protect this house."
uncertain: tóns-kʷe bʰoréyet: masc ACC.PL; either the guests ('waited on them') or the food (wheat masc + onions neut)
h₂éǵt: speaker unspecified (master or a guest)
ḱóm: deictic ACC.SG 'this' with dṓm, not the preposition

english: Earth, we give you wheat and barley. And honey and poured mead we offer. We offer you red apples. Great is your gift. Accept the gift; we are your praisers. Grant us offspring in spring. And may you be great and good.
uncertain: ǵʰutóm: neut ACC.SG 'poured' agreeing with médʰu (also AOR/IMP.2DU 'pour')
wésni: LOC 'in spring' (also LOC of 'sale')
tewóm dóh₃r̥ méǵh₂ h₁ésti: 'your gift' could mean Earth's gift to people or the offering

english: The king had a thousand cattle and a hundred horses; the shepherd had two cows. A harsh winter came. The king's thousand cattle died in the field. The shepherd led his two cows home alive. In spring the king came to that house. The shepherd gave him mead. The king drank it and rejoiced. He gave him a hundred sheep.
uncertain: h₃rēǵéy/poh₂imnéy + h₁sént/h₁stā́m: dative of possession
tr̥nóm: 'sharp, stiff' read as 'harsh' with neuter ǵʰéymn̥
gʷíh₃wom: see misfit; 'alive' supplied from context
misfit: gʷíh₃wom: parses only as PST.1SG 'I was living', which does not fit a 3rd-person narrative; the context wants the adjective 'alive' agreeing with the dual gʷówh₁ (ACC.DU gʷih₃wóh₁)

english: In spring the winter thaws, and the man yoked the oxen to the plough. Leading them, he ploughs the field. He grips the sturdy plough in his hands and sweats. Birds follow the plough. He sings a hymn. Then his wife sows the seed and covers it in the furrow. It rained. When the sun and the clouds had come, the grain grew, and his heart rejoiced.
uncertain: ǵʰéyōm: NOM.SG 'winter/snow' (also GEN.PL 'of horses')
tinéh₁ti: 'melts / comes to an end'
lóyseh₂: read as LOC 'in the furrow' (NOM also possible)
sóh₂wl̥-kʷe n̥bʰrós: -kʷe on the first conjunct after h₁yód
tense mix: PRS narration with AOR yéwgt

english: "Brother, where are you driving the sheep?" "I am driving them to the spring. The pasture is dry." "Have you seen the wild beast?" "No one has seen it. The dog heard it in the night." "Where do you live?" "I live by the marsh." "What are you carrying?" "I am carrying wool." "Brother, farewell! May the gods protect them."
uncertain: gʷíh₃we: IMP 'live!' used as farewell
sélesi h₁épi: LOC + postposition 'at the marsh'

english: Wheel of the sun, warm the field! Ripen the many ears of wheat. Wheel, do not burn the barley. Wheel, you are great; watch over it. Give heat to the wheat. Give us imperishable fame.
uncertain: h₁ím: masc = the field (h₂éǵros)
h₁éwsoyh₁s: OPT.2SG with mē, negative wish
misfit: h₂élbʰitih₁: parses only as NOM/ACC dual 'two barleys' (neuter i-stem), which makes no sense for a mass noun as object of 'burn'; expected ACC.SG h₂élbʰit

english: It was getting dark. The sheep were lying in the fold. Then a wolf came out of the darkness. Then it crept toward them. They trembled. The ram stood up in front. His two eyes were red. The wolf seized him. Then the dog came. The wolf let him go and fled. The ram's wool was red with blood. The ram survived.
uncertain: h₁ésyo h₃ókʷih₁: 'his eyes'; could be the ram's or the wolf's
h₁íh₂n̥s sérpet: bare ACC of goal 'crept toward them'
gʷíh₃wet: PST 'was alive', read as 'survived'

english: The sheep said to the horses: "It pains my heart to see a man driving horses."
uncertain: entire text: translated from recognition of Schleicher's fable, not from the tools
misfit: entire item (awis, akwabʰyams, ā, wawakat, kard, agʰnutai, mai, widanti, manum, akwams, agantam): written in Schleicher's 1868 laryngeal-less reconstruction, not the corpus notation; the analyzer returns no analysis for any token

english: The master said to his son: "I give you the cattle. I give you the fields. Plough it! Guard them! Do not cheat your brother. Do not steal. Its boundary is firm. Remember the oath. May your fame be good."
uncertain: tóns: masc.pl = the cattle
h₁ésyo térmn̥: 'its boundary', singular, again pointing back to a single field
pótis: 'master/husband'; read as the father
misfit: h₁ím: masc ACC.SG 'it' as object of 'plough', but its only antecedent is plural h₂éǵrons 'fields'; expected h₁íns, or else singular h₂éǵrom
